newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvians haunted by year of disasters.
newsitem.headline: Peruvians haunted by year of disasters.

text.p: A mudslide that buried between 250 and 300 Andean peasants is the latest in a string of disasters to blight Peru in the last year.
A grim litany of plane crashes, horrific accidents and earthquakes -- plus continuing guerrilla activity including the 65-day Lima hostage crisis -- have left Peruvians stunned.
The following is a list of disasters in the last 12 months:
-- Feb. 18, 1997 - A massive mudslide in the Andes in southeastern Peru sweeps over two villages, burying between 250 and 300 people and leaving scores more homeless.
-- Nov. 12, 1996 - An earthquake in southern Peru kills 14, injures hundreds and leaves tens of thousands homeless.
-- Oct. 2, 1996 - An Aeroperu Boeing 757 jet plunges into the Pacific off Peru, killing all 70 on board.
-- Aug. 14, 1996 - Thirty-five people die from electrocution and 40 are injured when fireworks strike a high-voltage electricity cable in the southern city of Arequipa.
-- Feb. 29, 1996 - A Peruvian Faucett airline Boeing 737 crashes in the Andes, killing all 117 passengers and six crew.
-- 1996 - Around 400 people, mainly peasants, died in a series of bus crashes on remote Andean roads.
